- When sentiment is positive (≥0.25) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.00) or flat, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5–10% in 1–2 days); apply dampening factor of 0.85–0.90 to peak forecasts.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, forecast should not drop below 10% below recent 7-day low.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate in early period (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or negative — add 0.5–1.5% buffer.
- If sentiment history shows rising optimism (e.g., 0.00 → 0.67 → 1.00), model often overreacts — cap forecast increase at 3–5% above prior peak.
- Avoid extrapolating sentiment-driven momentum beyond 10–15 days — sentiment decay often causes forecast divergence after 14 days.
